title: Piggy bank: retired DDR4 DIMMs reborn on CXL expander cards
idea: The 'piggy bank' of savings is the DDR4 sitting in decommissioned servers. Design a PCIe/CXL card around an off-the-shelf CXL memory controller ASIC that hosts 8 used DDR4 RDIMMs, plus a burn-in and test flow, and sell it as a capacity tier. Board design and pilot runs fit within $1M.
why: Cost per bit and supply: reused bits cost roughly 10-20% of new DDR5 and need zero new wafers.
note: Already deployed by hyperscalers (CXL DDR4 reuse); straightforward but not novel.

title: Taffy-pulled wire-in-glass preform sliced into through-glass-via wafers
idea: Stack copper-cored glass capillaries into a preform, draw it down 500x on a fiber tower, re-bundle and redraw (as multicore fiber is made), then slice the rod like salami into 100 um glass discs. Each disc holds millions of 2 um-pitch through-glass vias formed in one draw.
why: Laser drilling plus plating of glass vias is slow and costly; drawing yields interposer cores with ~10^7 vias/cm2 at fiber-tower throughput, for denser and cheaper memory interposers.
note: Taylor-wire drawing of Cu-in-glass is real; via registration to pads and Cu/glass CTE are the doubts.

title: Bookshelf memory: dies stand on edge atop compute
idea: Eliminate both the interposer and TSVs: route top-metal lines to a polished, metallized die edge carrying ~2 um-pitch pads, stand dozens of DRAM dies vertically on the GPU's top surface and hybrid-bond their edges; the gaps between the standing dies become microfluidic coolant channels, so the memory doubles as a heat-sink fin array.
why: A 10 mm x 100 um edge offers ~250k contacts per die (more than a whole HBM stack) with zero TSV area and no interposer; vertical wire length <100 um targets <0.3 pJ/bit vs 3-4 pJ/bit HBM and attacks the TSV tax.
note: Huge edge contact count with no TSVs; polished-edge 2 um pads and mechanical stability are major unknowns.

title: Hadamard-spread embedding storage turns bit flips into faint Gaussian noise
idea: Shift the unit of meaning from bits to whole vectors: embeddings are stored after a fixed Hadamard rotation and spread-spectrum quantization, so any 1% of flipped bits perturb every coordinate slightly instead of wrecking a few; the inverse transform runs in the near-memory logic die as data streams out.
why: Lets the largest AI capacity consumers (recommendation tables, retrieval indexes, KV caches) live in no-ECC 1%-BER memory with negligible accuracy loss, ~2x lower cost per usable bit.
note: Spreading equalizes but does not shrink MSB-flip error energy; value depends on cheap high-BER DRAM existing.

title: Discarding and recovering: partial-good HBM stacks sold as lower tiers
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: instead of scrapping stacks with one bad tier or weak TSV lanes, fuse out the bad tier or half the lanes in the base die and re-bin the stacks as 8-high or half-width parts for inference cards and edge devices. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)
why: HBM yield (fact 6): turns the 20-30% yield loss into a sellable lower tier, effectively +10-20% usable HBM supply from the same wafers.

title: Map-tile mipmapped KV cache: zoom only where needed
idea: Map apps load coarse tiles, then zoom in. Keep pooled summary keys for each 64-token block in HBM and score those blocks first. Full-resolution KV blocks come from CXL or flash only for the highest-scoring tiles.
why: Long-context KV caches fill most of HBM. Tile-based fetch could shrink the HBM KV footprint 4-8x with little accuracy loss.
note: Quest/InfLLM-style block summary keys already published.

title: Automata Processor fixed: one hard-wired in-DRAM job, KV-cache top-k filtering
idea: Micron's Automata Processor died because nobody wanted to program NFAs and DRAM-process logic was slow. Hard-wire one function with a huge market: each bank's sense-amp stripe computes 4-bit dot products of a broadcast query against the open row of keys and returns only the indices of the top-k matches, so the accelerator fetches just those KV entries through one new command and no programming model.
why: Overfetch and data movement (facts 5, 8): long-context attention moves 10-30x less KV data off-chip, using bank-level parallelism for TB/s internal bandwidth.
note: Bank-level top-k cuts long-context KV traffic 10-30x; area in the sense-amp stripe and approximate-attention accuracy are doubts.

title: Memory-side top-k gate returns token indices, not keys
idea: Eliminate shipping full key vectors: each HBM pseudo-channel's base-die slice holds a small dot-product unit and comparator tree that scores the query against stored keys inside the stack and returns only the top-k token indices; only those value rows then cross the interface.
why: Long-context KV reads dominate decode bandwidth; for k=64 of 128k tokens interface traffic falls >10x for ~3-5% base-die area.

title: Idle chat sessions keep tokens, not KV caches, until resumed
idea: A KV entry is ~100-500 KB per token but the token that produced it is 2 bytes, and most KV memory belongs to sessions idle between user turns. Evict idle sessions to token IDs only and re-prefill them on return using cheap older-node recompute chiplets, trading FLOPs for bytes.
why: Resident KV memory falls 100x+ for typical chat duty cycles; trades resume latency and prefill energy.

title: Hash-deduplicating base die stores shared KV prefixes once
idea: Worsen: store the same system-prompt KV cache separately for every user. Flip: the memory base die hashes each 4 KB block on write and keeps a content-addressed table, so identical prefix blocks across users map to one physical copy with copy-on-write, transparent to the host.
why: Usable capacity: 2-5x more effective KV capacity per GB for chat inference with shared prompts and agents.
note: Prefix sharing already done in host software (vLLM); hardware dedup adds modest novelty.

title: Astronomy CCD correlated double sampling enables 20 mV memory links
idea: Astronomical CCDs read single electrons by correlated double sampling, subtracting a reset sample from the signal sample. Put clocked CDS receivers on interposer/TSV links so offsets and low-frequency noise cancel, allowing 20-30 mV swings driven from a dedicated switched-capacitor 0.1 V rail.
why: Line energy ~C*Vswing*Vrail: 30 mV swing from a 0.1 V rail vs 0.4 V links cuts wire energy >10x, attacking data-movement energy and the voltage floor at the interface.
note: CDS cancels offsets enabling ~30 mV swings; clocking overhead and settling at speed are the doubt.

title: Via-ROM weight chiplet: frozen weights need no DRAM
idea: Eliminate DRAM, its writes and its refresh for deployed model weights: encode weights in a single custom via-mask layer of a mature-node ROM die (one via = one bit) hybrid-bonded under the compute die; the data survives power loss by construction.
why: Weights are ~60-80% of inference memory; via-ROM is ~5x cheaper per bit than DRAM, needs one 28-40 nm mask (no EUV, U.S.-fabbable) and reads at ~0.1 pJ/bit over hybrid bonds.
note: Mature-node via-ROM is ~10x less dense than DRAM; only frozen models; Taalas-like hardwiring exists.
